exposure: External pressure applied to chest wall (-6, 0, or +6 cmH2O)
Simulated lung liquid volume (drained for control/vaginal delivery, 30 ml/kg returned for elevated liquid/caesarean section)
cohort: Near-term rabbit kittens (30 days gestational age, term ~31 days) at risk of developing respiratory distress.
finding: External negative pressures increased lung aeration and resulted in a more evenly distributed tidal ventilation immediately after birth in near-term rabbit kittens, whereas external positive pressures reduced lung aeration and compliance.
mod_finding: External negative pressure increased functional residual capacity levels in both control kittens (simulating vaginal delivery) and elevated liquid kittens (simulating caesarean section).
